description: The lenses: ways of reading any object (a person, event, office, polity, place) from one dimension, by a specialist lens agent grounded per polity, or across all dimensions by the general lens. A lens is never stored in the graph (D-039, D-063): `predicates` says which registry predicates a lens highlights when it is on; `questions` and `relevance` are the analyst's brief (31 §3.3). Drafted by Claude acting as the agent, 2026-10-21, for the curator to review; the pilot on Actium decides which lenses are kept.

lenses.label: General
lenses.purpose: Reads the object across every dimension at once: its significance, how the dimensions act on each other, and what the specialists missed or duplicated.
lenses.relevance: Everything is in scope; the general lens judges what matters most and why.
questions: Why does this object matter, and to whom: contemporaries, later Romans, modern historians?
Where do the dimensions act on each other (a military means to a political end, an economic cause of a social change)?
Which of the specialists' findings and gaps are the same question asked twice?
What does no specialist lens cover?
Where do the sources disagree in a way that changes the reading in more than one dimension?
What should be read next, overall, and in what order?

lenses.label: Military
lenses.purpose: Armed force: its organization, command, use, supply, and consequences.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns forces (land or sea), who held authority over them and who actually commanded, operations and tactics, manpower and recruitment, logistics, losses, and what became of soldiers and veterans.
questions: Which forces took part, of what size and composition, according to whom?
Who held formal authority over each force, and who exercised command in the field or at sea?
What were the strategy, the operations, and the tactics, and how do the sources explain the outcome?
How were the forces raised, paid, supplied, and moved?
What were the losses, surrenders, and defections?
What happened to the forces afterwards: discharge, settlement, incorporation, garrisons?

lenses.label: Political
lenses.purpose: Power and its legitimacy: offices, powers, factions, decisions, and the constitution.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns who held which office or power and by what right, alliances and oppositions, decisions and the body that made them, propaganda and declarations, diplomacy, and constitutional change.
questions: Who held which offices and powers at the time, and how legitimate were they held to be, by whom?
Which factions, alliances, and oppositions were in play, and when did they shift?
Which decisions were taken, by which body (Senate, assemblies, magistrates, triumvirs, kings)?
How was the conflict framed in public: declarations, oaths, propaganda?
What diplomacy with client kings, allies, and foreign states was involved?
What changed in the constitution or the distribution of power because of it?

lenses.label: Economic
lenses.purpose: Resources: money, land, supply, production, and trade.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns financing (taxes, levies, requisitions, treasuries, loans), coinage, land and property, supply of grain and materials, trade and its disruption, booty, indemnities, and confiscations.
questions: How was it financed, and who paid?
What coinage was struck for it, by whom, and what does it show?
What land or property changed hands: confiscation, settlement, grants?
How were grain and materials supplied, and what disrupted supply?
What wealth was gained or lost: booty, treasuries, tribute, indemnities?
What lasting economic change followed?

lenses.label: Social
lenses.purpose: People in relation: kinship, patronage, status, loyalty, and the experience of ordinary participants.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns family and marriage ties, patrons and clients, status groups (senators, equestrians, freedmen, slaves, provincials), loyalty and defection, gender, and how soldiers, rowers, and civilians lived through it.
questions: Which kinship and marriage ties bound or divided the participants?
Which patrons and clients, friends and dependants, were involved?
Which status groups took part, and how did their position change?
Who changed sides, and what do the sources say moved them?
How did ordinary participants (soldiers, rowers, civilians) experience it?
How do the sources treat women and foreigners in it, and what does that show?

lenses.label: Religious
lenses.purpose: The gods and their human side: omens, vows, priesthoods, rituals, dedications, and divine claims.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns omens and portents, vows and their fulfilment, priesthoods held, rituals (including the declaration of war), temples, dedications, games and festivals, divine associations claimed by the participants, and commemoration.
questions: Which omens, portents, and prophecies do the sources report, and to what end?
Which vows, dedications, temples, or games are tied to it?
Which priesthoods did the participants hold, and did ritual frame the war or its end?
Which gods did the participants associate themselves with, and how was that used?
How was it commemorated in religious terms afterwards?

lenses.label: Archaeological
lenses.purpose: Material remains: sites, finds, stratigraphy, and what excavation shows.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns a site, excavation, finds (wrecks, rams, inscriptions on stone, coins as objects), building remains, or a phase dated by material evidence.
questions: What material remains bear on it, and where are they?
What has excavation or survey found, and when?
Does the material evidence confirm, correct, or contradict the texts?
How are the remains dated?

lenses.label: Artistic
lenses.purpose: Art and architecture: images, monuments, styles, and what they were made to say.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns a monument, statue, relief, painting, coin type as image, building programme, or the artistic representation of a person or event.
questions: What monuments or images commemorate or depict it?
Who commissioned them, and to what end?
How did the representation change over time?
What style or programme do they belong to?

lenses.label: Biographic
lenses.purpose: Lives: birth, family, careers, offices held, and death.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns a person's life events, family and marriages, offices and commands held, honours, exile, or death.
questions: Who took part, and what were their careers to that point?
What family ties or marriages bear on it?
What offices, commands, or honours did they hold?
What became of them afterwards?

lenses.label: Cultural
lenses.purpose: Identity and symbols: customs, values, and how a people saw itself and others.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns identity (Roman, Greek, Egyptian, eastern), customs, values, symbols, festivals, or cultural contrast and stereotype.
questions: What identities or values were invoked?
How were outsiders portrayed?
What customs or symbols were at stake?
What cultural change followed?

lenses.label: Demographic
lenses.purpose: People in numbers: population, manpower, migration, and settlement.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns numbers of people (armies, crews, casualties, populations), recruitment pools, colonists and veterans settled, migration, or urban growth.
questions: How many people were involved, and on what evidence?
Where did the manpower come from?
Who was settled or displaced, and where?
What did losses or settlement do to populations?

lenses.label: Diplomatic
lenses.purpose: Relations between powers: alliances, client kings, treaties, embassies.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns allies and client rulers, treaties, embassies, defections between sides, or the settlement of kingdoms and cities after a conflict.
questions: Which powers and rulers were allied with whom?
Who defected, and on what terms?
What treaties or settlements followed?
How did relations with client kingdoms change?

lenses.label: Environmental
lenses.purpose: Nature's part: climate, season, weather, disease, and the land itself.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns season, weather, wind and sea state, water supply, marsh and disease, harvests, or environmental change.
questions: What season and weather bore on it?
Did water, disease, or terrain affect the outcome?
What did the environment allow or forbid?
Did it change the landscape?

lenses.label: Geographic
lenses.purpose: Place and space: terrain, routes, regions, and territorial extent.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns where things happened, terrain and coastline, harbours and straits, routes and distances, regions, or the territory a power held.
questions: Where exactly did it happen, and what was the terrain?
What routes, harbours, or chokepoints mattered?
How did geography shape strategy and supply?
What territory changed hands?

lenses.label: Intellectual
lenses.purpose: Ideas and learning: philosophy, scholarship, and how thinkers explained events.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns philosophical or scholarly ideas, schools, education, historiographical method, or how ancient and modern thinkers explained an event.
questions: What ideas or schools of thought bear on it?
How did contemporary or later thinkers explain it?
What intellectual change followed?

lenses.label: Linguistic
lenses.purpose: Language and script: the words used, names, translations, and inscriptions' language.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns the language of sources or inscriptions, names and their forms, terms of art (Latin, Greek), translation, or bilingualism.
questions: In what language is the evidence, and what do its key terms mean?
How are names given and varied?
Does translation change the sense?

lenses.label: Scientific
lenses.purpose: Knowledge of nature: astronomy, medicine, calendars, and engineering knowledge.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns calendars and dating, astronomy and omens read astronomically, medicine, or technical knowledge as knowledge.
questions: What scientific knowledge bears on it (calendar, astronomy, medicine)?
How do calendars fix its date?
What did contemporaries know that shaped it?

lenses.label: Technological
lenses.purpose: Tools and techniques: ships, weapons, engineering, and their capabilities.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns ship types and sizes, rams and artillery, fortifications and siege works, roads and bridges, or a technique's capability and limits.
questions: What ships, weapons, or engineering were used?
What could they do, and what were their limits?
Did technology decide the outcome?
What technical change followed?

lenses.label: Communication
lenses.purpose: Messages and narratives: propaganda, ceremony, rumour, and how events were told and transmitted.
lenses.relevance: In scope when it concerns propaganda, speeches, letters, ceremonies and triumphs, rumours, oaths, or how a claim or event was transmitted and reshaped.
questions: How was it announced, celebrated, or justified?
Whose narrative prevailed, and how was it spread?
What rumours, speeches, or letters shaped it?
How was the story transmitted to later writers?

catalogued: Lenses with status 'catalogued' (2026-11-17, Claude, from Facets/facet_registry_master.json, for the curator to review) tag notes and are named in triage; they read nothing until a grounding for the scope exists, and coverage does not count them.
